title: Canonical-path-only dedup lets a tool-runtime visit suppress later link-library admission
status: CONFIRMED in the frozen source; live role-aware fix is under construction and requires a later exact-source review.
severity: Required dependency-admission boundary gap; must be fixed before relying on complete full-content link-library binding.
discovered_by: Backend author while implementing session-local trusted-tool identity memoization; independently confirmed by this reviewer against git show of the affected frozen commit.
source_trace: Inputs.seen is BTreeSet<PathBuf>. Inputs::file inserts the canonical path and returns early if present, before branching on its script boolean role.

Final-link key collection first identifies clang/linker and their ldd-reported runtime DSOs with file(path,false). That role uses the trusted-installed-tool model (GNU build ID plus metadata, content fallback), then returns.

An actual link library or script member later visits the same canonical file with file(path,true). The old seen set returns success immediately, omitting fs::read/full bytes, MAX_FILE admission, ELF/archive/script parsing and DT_NEEDED collection. libc.so.6 and the loader can have these overlapping roles.
correction_to_prior_claim: Earlier source receipts remain unmodified historical artifacts. Their general statement that link libraries/scripts always bind complete current bytes was too broad for this overlapping-path case; do not carry that statement forward without the role-aware fix.
evidence_limits: This establishes the skipped required byte/admission path, not an independently demonstrated stale ELF in the controlled installed native toolchain. Existing trusted-tool metadata/build-ID identity still binds the first role; it must not silently substitute for the distinct raw-library admission contract.
required_fix: Deduplicate by canonical path plus admission role, or otherwise ensure a later stronger library role performs its full checks even after a tool-runtime visit.

Add a regression that first accepts file(false) and then requires the same path to execute and fail the stronger file(true) admission for unsupported library content. A key-only difference or ordinary native success does not prove this boundary.

Keep link-library payload hashing and parsing outside trusted-tool metadata memoization; instrument actual library bytes/calls independently of tool identity fallback bytes if claiming their current work.
reviewer_actions: Read-only frozen-source and live-diff review only; no build, compiler invocation, benchmark, production/helper modification or commit.
